sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: ECBC is notified by the Central Government under the **Energy Conservation Act, 2001**.
• **Primary Objective**: To optimize building design to reduce energy consumption, specifically targeting **HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning)**, lighting, and electrical systems.
• **Scope**: Applicable to commercial buildings with a connected load of **100kW** or contract demand of **120kVA**.
• **Key Metric**: **Energy Performance Index (EPI)**, measured in kWh/sq.m/year, which serves as the benchmark for building efficiency.

Architectural design that uses natural sources (sun, wind) to maintain thermal comfort, reducing reliance on mechanical systems.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Star Rating Program**: BEE's rating system for existing buildings based on actual energy performance.
• **Smart Cities Mission**: Integration of ECBC standards in urban planning to create energy-efficient infrastructure.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of mandatory enforcement by State Governments, high initial capital cost, and shortage of trained energy auditors.
• **Solutions**: Incentivizing green buildings through 'Floor Area Ratio' (FAR) bonuses and mandatory compliance in municipal building bylaws.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'BEE-L-E-C' (BEE, Load, Envelope, Comfort).
• **Decoded Meaning**: BEE (Authority) sets standards for Load (100kW), Envelope (Design), and Comfort (HVAC/Lighting).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'ECBC' as being mandatory for all buildings. It is currently mandatory for commercial buildings above a specific load, but adoption for residential buildings is largely voluntary/state-dependent.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Decarbonization of the Built Environment' to describe the role of ECBC in achieving India's Net Zero 2070 target.

keyTakeaways: ECBC is a statutory instrument under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) is the nodal agency for implementation.
EPI (Energy Performance Index) is the primary metric for measuring building efficiency.
